description: Neutralizes the dot-notation traversal guard at _FrameworkController.cs:513-516 (`if (field.Contains('.')) return BadRequest("Navigation property paths are not allowed for inline editing");`) with a compile-preserving operator (`field.Contains('.') && false`, not a deletion) so the condition can never be true. Checked against UpdateModelProperty_DotNotationField_ReturnsBadRequest, which submits field="Photo.FileName" against a real seeded FrameworkUser. With the guard neutralized, the request still returns 400 -- 'Photo.FileName' is not a legal CLR member name, so it falls through to the unrelated property-existence check a few lines later (_FrameworkController.cs, `entityType.GetProperty(field, ...)` returning null) and gets 'Field not found or not writable' instead. Status-code-only assertions cannot tell those two 400s apart; the test's second assertion (the response body must contain 'Navigation property paths are not allowed') is what actually pins this guard, and is exactly what goes red here. green_tests are UpdateModelProperty_PasswordField_ReturnsBadRequest and UpdateModelProperty_ITCodeField_ReturnsBadRequest, proving blast-radius scoping in the other direction from mvc004-blocklist-empty-http-blindspot: neutralizing the dot-notation guard has no effect on the independent blockedFields check.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.MvcAuthHolesTes: the 400 must come from the dot-notation guard specifically.*Got body: Field not found or not writable

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout with the mutant patch applied: 'Assert.IsTrue failed. MVC-004: the 400 must come from the dot-notation guard specifically (its message), not from the unrelated property-existence check that would ALSO 400 a literal "Photo.FileName" property lookup if the dot-notation guard were deleted. Got body: Field not found or not writable'.
